transcript:
Header: 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood CSM), Sara Kim (Crestview Head of Security), Ethan Li (Cloud Architect), Priya Rao (Privacy Counsel), Marcus Young (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): security and privacy deep-dive focused on data handling, retention, PII/PHI controls, encryption/KMS, and confirmation that customer content is not used to train public models. Action items captured.

00:00:05 - Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on this account. Diego will cover the technical controls, and Nina's on for any CSM/ops questions.
00:00:15 - Sara: Thanks. We wanted to cover SOC2, ISO, encryption, key management, and a big one for legal - retention and whether customer prompts are used to train models.
00:00:24 - Diego: Yep totally, we'll walk through our hosted vs dedicated vs private options and the related controls. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, data residency and retention, and then the training on data question.
00:00:40 - Ethan: Sounds good. We are particularly focused on PII/PHI handling since Crestview is a healthcare SaaS - HIPAA in scope.
00:00:48 - Avery: Understood. Quick note - we have a BAA process and Redwood Private option for full customer-managed network.

05:12 - Diego: SOC 2 type II - we maintain an annual attestation, you can see scope items in the report. ISO 27001 we have an inbound cert and summary; I'll attach the short version after. Our security controls include least-privilege RBAC in the console and API keys, SSO via SAML/SCIM for enterprise accounts, and optional just-in-time access for ops.
05:34 - Priya: On RBAC - can we map roles to our internal groups? We want separation between dev and prod ops.
05:40 - Diego: Yes, you can map via SAML group sync and custom roles in the console. We also have session-level admin approvals for sensitive actions.

08:02 - Avery: Audit logs - we emit detailed audit trails for API key usage, model deployments, and user logins. Logs are exportable to your SIEM (SPLUNK/Datadog) via secure forwarder.
08:18 - Marcus: Do logs include partial prompt text? We want to avoid storing PHI in logs.
08:25 - Diego: Good question. By default, audit metadata includes request IDs, model used, latency, and token counts. Full prompt text is not included in system audit logs unless debug mode is enabled or you opt into request logging for troubleshooting. When request logging is enabled, request bodies can be written to debug logs with redaction hooks. We also provide an opt-out flag at the project level to never persist request content.

12:05 - Sara: So to be clear - if we use hosted Redwood API and do not enable request logging, Redwood will not retain the prompt/content?
12:12 - Avery: For hosted by default we retain minimal telemetry and metrics. We have configurable retention windows for request/response content; default retention for content is 30 days but for enterprise customers we can contract a shorter window or disable retention entirely. Also Dedicated deployments have separate tenancy - in Dedicated we can configure no-content retention and we can set up private networking.
12:37 - Priya: Is there a written SLA or contractual term that says 'no training on customer data'? That's important for us - legal needs explicit non-training language.
12:46 - Diego: We have explicit contract language: Redwood does not use customer-provided data to train our public models. For hosted API, data may be used for internal debugging/quality with explicit opt-in; for enterprise contracts we can add a non-training clause and set retention to zero. For Private deployments, you control the environment entirely and there is no data exfiltration to Redwood training systems.
12:58 - Sara: Do you have a short plain-language statement we can include in our vendor risk assessment?
13:03 - Avery: Yes - I'll send the vendor statement: 'Redwood does not use customer prompts, responses, or files to train or improve public models. Customer data may be retained for diagnostic purposes within configurable retention windows and can be disabled by contract.'

18:30 - Ethan: Encryption - is data encrypted in transit and at rest? How do keys work?
18:36 - Diego: TLS 1.2+ in transit. At rest we use envelope encryption. For hosted, keys are managed in our KMS; we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS or GCP KMS for enterprise customers. Key rotation is supported and logged. For Private deployments, you can plug in your HSM/KMS.
18:55 - Marcus: Is there an HSM-backed KMS option for Dedicated?
19:00 - Diego: Yes, Dedicated + Private both have HSM options. We can provide architecture diagrams showing key flow.

22:11 - Sara: Data residency - we need logs and content to remain in EU for some customers. Can you guarantee regional residency?
22:20 - Avery: Yes, we have region pins and can route data to EU-hosted clusters. For Hosted we offer EU regions and we will contract residency for accounts. For Private you deploy into your VPC in the region of your choice.

26:05 - Priya: Regarding retention and eDiscovery - if a customer sends PHI in a prompt, what's the lifecycle? How do we ensure it can be removed?
26:15 - Diego: We support subject access and deletion requests. If content is stored, we can delete request/response artifacts in-line and provide a deletion confirmation. For Hosted, if you enable opt-out for retention at the project level or use a Dedicated setup with zero-retention config, the content won't be stored beyond ephemeral processing. We also provide logs that show deletion operations for audit trails.

29:40 - Sara: HIPAA - you said BAA is available. Does Redwood sign a standard BAA and is Private deployment required?
29:50 - Avery: We can sign a BAA. For Hosted HIPAA use we generally recommend Dedicated or Private so you have stronger isolation and contractual controls, but we do support HIPAA controls for enterprise hosted customers under a BAA with strict retention and logging settings.

33:02 - Marcus: A technical question - does Redwood ever surface customer prompt fragments in shared model telemetry or aggregated datasets?
33:10 - Diego: No. Aggregated telemetry is statistical (latency histograms, token distributions). We do not include customer prompt text in model telemetry. Any text included for debugging is a deliberate opt-in and redacted unless you grant access.

36:48 - Priya: For our vendor risk reviews we need evidence: SOC2 report, encryption diagram, KMS config, BAA template, and your 'no training' statement.
36:55 - Avery: We'll bundle those docs and send them after the call.

39:20 - Ethan: Performance/observability - if we do a limited pilot, can we run internal traffic through a Dedicated pool so we measure latency and also validate logs?
39:31 - Diego: Yep, we can spin up a Dedicated pilot with a small reserved pool. That gives you isolated perf metrics, and we can enable SIEM forwarding of audit logs for the pilot.

42:05 - Sara: A couple of red flags we watch for: long default retention, no exportable logs, and vendor training of customer data. It sounds like Redwood has mitigations but we need them written in the contract.
42:17 - Avery: Totally - we'll include contract language for retention windows, data usage (no training), and exportability of logs. We'll also include the option to use CMKs and HSM for key control.

45:00 - Marcus: Small nit - we've seen transcriptions where 'KV cache' was transcribed as 'K V cash' and some other mis-parses; just flagging that for internal ops when we search logs.
45:10 - Diego: Yep, transcripts can be messy, we rely on structured telemetry for exact metrics.

46:20 - Avery: Recap: send SOC2/ISO docs, security whitepaper, BAA, non-training vendor statement, encryption/KMS diagram, sample retention config. Schedule follow-up infra deep-dive (Diego + Marcus + Ethan). Customer to confirm regulatory controls list.
46:40 - Sara: Thanks, this was helpful. We'll review the docs and aim to set up the pilot if everything checks out.

47:58 - Avery: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the bundle.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker overlaps typical of Fireflies exports. References to attachments: [SOC2_report.pdf], [Encryption_KMS_diagram.png], [BAA_draft.docx], [security_whitepaper.pdf].
